messages.subject: Python/Jupyter case study: hierarchical home radon model
parts:
Chris Fonnesebck (of PyMC fame) kindly contributed a Jupyter notebook
he created as a demo for PyStan (for the short course Chris, Daniel, and
I just taught at Vanderbilt). It's not only a good introduction
to PyStan and a good example of how to use Jupyter, it's a good
introduction to Stan and hierarchical modeling. And it replicates
one of Andrew's favorite teaching examples---home radon level estimation
and prediction.

Here's the abstract I wrote for it:

This case study replicates the analysis of home radon levels using
hierarchical models of Lin, Gelman, Price, and Kurtz (1999).
It illustrates how to generalize linear regressions to hierarchical
models with group-level predictors and how to compare predictive inferences
and evaluate model fits. Along the way it shows how to get data into Stan
using pandas, how to sample using PyStan, and how to visualize the results
using Seaborn.

You can find the link to the source repo and the rendered HTML
on our case studies page:

http://mc-stan.org/documentation/case-studies.html

Thanks, Chris!

- Bob
